entries.title: QUANTEC: Normal Tissue Effects in the Central Nervous System (Brain, Brainstem, Spinal Cord, Optic Apparatus, Cochlea)
entries.organization: American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM) / ASTRO

organ_constraints.notes: Data at 72 and 90 Gy show 5% and 10% risk, extrapolated from BED models. Keep Dmax < 60 Gy for partial brain irradiation.
Volume of normal brain receiving >= 12 Gy should be < 5-10 cc. Rapid rise in symptomatic radionecrosis when V12 > 5-10 cc.
Whole brainstem dose constraint. Small subvolume (D1-10cc) <= 59 Gy has < 5% risk. Point dose (< 0.1-1 cc) Dmax < 64 Gy has < 5% risk.
Single fraction SRS point dose limit, derived primarily from acoustic neuroma / vestibular schwannoma series.
Dmax 55-60 Gy carries 3-7% risk; Dmax > 60 Gy carries > 7-20% risk. For pituitary adenomas, tolerance may be lower. Strict limit < 54 Gy commonly used.
Single fraction SRS constraint. Many centres enforce conservative Dmax < 8-10 Gy to optic chiasm in single fraction.
Full cross section of cord irradiated to 50 Gy has 0.2% myelopathy risk; 60 Gy has 6% risk; 69 Gy has 50% risk. Standard clinical constraint is Dmax <= 45-50 Gy.
Single fraction spine SBRT with partial cross-section. Cord Dmax <= 13 Gy or D0.03cc <= 14 Gy has ~1% myelopathy risk.
3-fraction spine SBRT. Partial cord cross-section Dmax <= 20 Gy carries ~1% myelopathy risk.
Mean cochlear dose <= 45 Gy maintains risk of SNHL < 30%. Sparing to Mean < 30-35 Gy strongly recommended, particularly with concurrent cisplatin.

organ_constraints.endpoint: Sensorineural hearing loss / loss of serviceable hearing
organ_constraints.notes: Single fraction acoustic neuroma / vestibular schwannoma SRS. Prescription dose <= 14 Gy keeps loss of serviceable hearing < 25%.

key_passages.text: For partial brain irradiation using conventional fractionation (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx), Dmax < 60 Gy is associated with < 3% risk of symptomatic necrosis. Higher doses of 72 Gy and 90 Gy yield 5% and 10% necrosis risk.
Myelopathy risk after full cross-section cord irradiation is 0.2% at 50 Gy, 6% at 60 Gy, and 50% at 69 Gy. In single-fraction SRS, Dmax <= 13 Gy carries ~1% risk.
Optic neuropathy risk is < 3% for Dmax < 55 Gy, 3-7% for 55-60 Gy, and > 7-20% for > 60 Gy. Single fraction SRS threshold is Dmax < 12 Gy.

entries.title: QUANTEC: Normal Tissue Effects in the Head & Neck (Salivary Glands, Pharyngeal Constrictors, Larynx)

organ_constraints.notes: Combined bilateral parotid mean dose < 25 Gy preserves stimulated salivary output. Bilateral mean < 39 Gy has < 50% risk.
If one parotid gland receives substantial dose, sparing the contralateral single parotid gland to mean dose < 20 Gy ensures < 20% long-term xerostomia.
Mean constrictor dose < 50 Gy correlates with < 20% symptomatic dysphagia and aspiration risk. Sparing larynx and constrictors reduces long-term gastrostomy tube dependence.
In combined chemoradiation, keeping whole larynx Dmax < 66 Gy prevents severe vocal dysfunction. Mean larynx dose < 50 Gy prevents aspiration (< 30%).
Without concurrent chemotherapy, larynx mean dose < 44 Gy or V50 < 27% limits symptomatic edema risk to < 20%.

key_passages.text: Severe xerostomia (stimulated flow < 25% baseline) is reduced to < 20% if bilateral parotid mean dose is < 25 Gy, or if at least one parotid is spared to mean dose < 20 Gy.
Mean dose to the pharyngeal constrictor muscles < 50 Gy reduces symptomatic dysphagia and aspiration to < 20%. Vocal cord dysfunction risk is < 20% if whole larynx Dmax < 66 Gy.

entries.title: QUANTEC: Normal Tissue Effects in the Thorax (Lungs, Esophagus, Heart)

organ_constraints.notes: Standard fractionation threshold. V20 <= 30-35% keeps pneumonitis < 20%. V5 should ideally be kept < 60-65% in IMRT plans.
Gradual dose-response curve: MLD 7 Gy = 5%, MLD 13 Gy = 10%, MLD 20 Gy = 20%, MLD 24 Gy = 30%, MLD 27 Gy = 40%.
In 3 to 5 fraction lung SBRT, V20 < 10% (or < 1000 cc receiving 13.5 Gy) is strongly protective against fatal pneumonitis.
Whole organ mean dose < 34 Gy limits severe acute esophagitis. Grade >= 2 esophagitis limits: V35 < 50%, V50 < 40%, V70 < 20% maintain risk < 30%.
Pericardium mean dose < 26 Gy and V30 < 46% maintain pericarditis rate < 15%.
Whole organ V25 < 10% is associated with long-term cardiac mortality < 1%. In modern breast RT, mean heart dose < 2-4 Gy recommended (7.4% relative excess major coronary events per Gy mean dose).

key_passages.text: Bilateral lung V20 <= 30-35% and mean lung dose (MLD) <= 20 Gy keep symptomatic radiation pneumonitis risk to <= 20%. MLD dose-response: 7 Gy (5%), 13 Gy (10%), 20 Gy (20%), 24 Gy (30%).
Mean esophageal dose < 34 Gy limits acute Grade >= 3 esophagitis to 5-20%. Grade >= 2 esophagitis correlates with V35 < 50%, V50 < 40%, V70 < 20%.
Pericardium mean dose < 26 Gy and V30 < 46% maintain pericarditis < 15%. Whole heart V25 < 10% is associated with long-term cardiac mortality < 1%.

entries.title: QUANTEC: Normal Tissue Effects in the Abdomen and GI (Liver, Stomach, Small Bowel, Kidneys)

organ_constraints.notes: In patients without pre-existing liver disease. Mean dose < 30-32 Gy gives < 5% RILD. Mean dose 42 Gy gives 50% RILD.
In patients with Child-Pugh A cirrhotic liver disease or HCC. Tolerance is significantly lower: Mean dose < 28 Gy gives < 5% RILD; Mean dose 36 Gy gives 50% RILD.
Critical normal tissue volume: at least 700 cc of normal liver must receive a total dose < 15 Gy in 3-5 fractions.
Bilateral kidneys mean dose < 15-18 Gy gives < 5% chronic renal failure. Mean dose 28 Gy gives 50% risk. Partial volume constraints: V12 < 55%, V20 < 32%, V23 < 30%, V28 < 20% have < 5% risk.
Whole organ D100% < 45 Gy gives < 7% ulceration risk. Absolute Dmax should be kept < 50-54 Gy.
When individual bowel loops are contoured: V15 < 120 cc gives < 10% severe acute toxicity. If entire peritoneal cavity space is contoured: V45 < 195 cc gives < 10% severe acute toxicity.

key_passages.text: Classic RILD risk is < 5% when mean liver dose < 30-32 Gy in non-cirrhotic patients, and < 28 Gy in Child-Pugh A cirrhosis. In liver SBRT, at least 700 cc normal liver must receive < 15 Gy.
Bilateral kidneys mean dose < 15-18 Gy maintains nephropathy risk < 5%. Partial volume thresholds: V12 < 55%, V20 < 32%, V28 < 20%.
Individual small bowel loops V15 < 120 cc keeps acute Grade >= 3 toxicity < 10%. Whole stomach D100% < 45 Gy keeps ulceration < 7%.

entries.title: QUANTEC: Normal Tissue Effects in the Pelvis (Rectum, Bladder, Penile Bulb, Femoral Heads)

organ_constraints.notes: Prostate radiotherapy dose-volume staircase: V50 < 50%, V60 < 35%, V65 < 25%, V70 < 20%, V75 < 15%. Enforcing this step-down maintains Grade >= 2 toxicity < 15% and Grade >= 3 toxicity < 10%.
Prostate radiotherapy (RTOG 0415 / QUANTEC): V65 <= 50%, V70 <= 35%, V75 <= 25%, V80 <= 15%. Bladder cancer definitive RT: Dmax < 65 Gy gives < 6% late Gr >= 3 toxicity.
Mean dose to 95% of penile bulb < 50 Gy or D90 < 50 Gy keeps severe erectile dysfunction < 35%. D60-70 < 70 Gy gives < 55% risk.
Keep V50 < 5-10% and Dmax < 52 Gy to prevent avascular necrosis and femoral neck fracture.

key_passages.text: Prostate radiotherapy rectal dose-volume staircase: V50 < 50%, V60 < 35%, V65 < 25%, V70 < 20%, V75 < 15% maintains late Grade >= 2 toxicity < 15% and Grade >= 3 < 10%.
Prostate radiotherapy bladder limits: V65 <= 50%, V70 <= 35%, V75 <= 25%, V80 <= 15%. Penile bulb mean dose to 95% of gland < 50 Gy preserves potency.

entries.title: PENTEC: Pediatric Normal Tissue Effects in the Brain, Cerebrovasculature, Optic Apparatus, Endocrine, and Cochlea

organ_constraints.notes: 59 Gy to any part carries 5% necrosis risk; 67 Gy carries 10% risk. Reirradiation composite EQD2/2 = 112 Gy carries 5% risk.

18 Gy to 100% brain has 5% risk of IQ < 85; 26 Gy to 100% brain has 20% risk. 36 Gy to 10% brain has 5% risk; 51 Gy to 10% brain has 20% risk. Methotrexate adds ~6 Gy whole-brain uniform dose equivalent.

organ_constraints.endpoint: Stroke / cerebral vasculopathy (Moyamoya) by attained age 35y

organ_constraints.notes: Retina Dmax 42 Gy has 5% risk of retinopathy; Dmax 62 Gy has 50% risk. Optic nerve/chiasm Dmax 57 Gy has 5% neuropathy; 64 Gy has 50%. Lens mean dose 9 Gy has 50% cataract risk.
GH axis is exquisitely radiosensitive. D100% 15 Gy gives 5% GH deficiency. Central hypothyroidism occurs at D100% 22 Gy (20% risk); ACTH deficiency occurs at D100% 34 Gy (20% risk).
Without concurrent/intrathecal chemo: D0.03cc < 54 Gy, D1cc < 50.4 Gy is safe. WITH CHEMOTHERAPY (especially intrathecal): threshold is lower: D0.03cc < 50.4 Gy, D1cc < 45 Gy.

organ_constraints.endpoint: Sensorineural hearing loss (>20 dB threshold shift)
organ_constraints.notes: Without chemo: Mean < 35 Gy gives < 5% risk, Mean 50 Gy gives 30% risk. Concurrent/cumulative cisplatin >= 300 mg/m2 shifts dose-response curve lower by ~7 Gy.

Mean 10 Gy gives 12% subclinical and 4% clinical hypothyroidism. Mean 20 Gy gives 25% subclinical and 7% clinical. Mean 30 Gy gives 44% subclinical and 13% clinical. Females have 1.7-fold higher risk than males.

key_passages.text: 59 Gy to any part of brain yields 5% necrosis risk. IQ < 85 risk is 5% at 18 Gy to 100% brain and 20% at 26 Gy. Methotrexate adds ~6 Gy whole-brain dose equivalent.
D100% 30 Gy to Circle of Willis carries ~1% stroke risk at age 35y; 45 Gy carries 2-3%; 54 Gy carries 3-4%.
Growth hormone deficiency threshold is D100% 15 Gy (5% risk). Cochlea mean dose < 35 Gy keeps hearing loss < 5%; cisplatin >= 300 mg/m2 lowers tolerance by ~7 Gy.

entries.title: PENTEC: Pediatric Normal Tissue Effects in Thorax, Abdomen, Pelvis, and Musculoskeletal System

organ_constraints.notes: V20 < 30% and Mean lung dose < 12 Gy give < 5% symptomatic pneumonitis. Late pneumonitis: V27 < 20% gives < 5% risk. In TBI: prescribed 11 Gy EQD2 has 3.6% idiopathic pneumonitis syndrome (IPS); 12 Gy EQD2 has 47.5% IPS.

Mean 20 Gy at 30y post-RT carries 1.1% HF, 2.1% CAD, 0.5% valvular disease. Anthracycline synergy: Mean 10 Gy + <250 mg/m2 cumulative anthracycline = 3.4% cardiac disease; Mean 10 Gy + >250 mg/m2 anthracycline = 4.8%.
D100% 10 Gy carries 6.1% risk of SOS; D100% 20 Gy carries 14.5% risk. Non-alkylating chemotherapy after whole-liver RT significantly increases toxicity.

organ_constraints.volume_spec: Whole kidneys (both kidneys in TBI/WAI, or solitary post-nephrectomy)
organ_constraints.notes: Hypertension: 9.6 Gy = 5% risk. Grade 2 CKD: 10.2 Gy = 5% risk. Grades 3-5 CKD: 14.5 Gy = 5% risk. Cisplatin synergy: RT + cisplatin V10 > 25% gives 5% risk. Ifosfamide synergy: RT + ifosfamide V10 > 40% gives 10% risk.

organ_constraints.endpoint: Clinically significant scoliosis and growth stunting
organ_constraints.notes: Age < 2y: > 10 Gy at risk. Age 2-6y: > 20 Gy at risk. Age > 6y: > 30 Gy at risk. Crucial: always irradiate entire vertebral body width uniformly to avoid asymmetric growth causing severe scoliosis.
Extremely vulnerable in young girls < 4y. Even 0.34-0.97 Gy carries 61% risk of severe hypoplasia; >= 0.97 Gy carries 97% risk. Block breast bud rigorously.
Germ cell epithelium is exceptionally sensitive: Mean > 1 Gy causes > 90% oligospermia. Leydig cells: Mean 0.2-12 Gy gives 25% low testosterone; Mean > 20 Gy gives 68% low testosterone.

Without chemo: < 10 Gy carries 12% POI by age 20y, 50% by age 40y. > 10 Gy carries 71% POI by age 20y, 100% by age 40y. Alkylator chemotherapy drastically worsens POI risk. Oophoropexy recommended if pelvis irradiated.

key_passages.text: Pediatric heart mean dose 20 Gy carries 3.8% risk of cardiac disease at 30y post-RT; anthracyclines synergize significantly. Lung V20 < 30% and mean < 12 Gy keep pneumonitis < 5%.

Vertebral bodies: threshold for scoliosis/growth stunting is > 10 Gy (age < 2y), > 20 Gy (2-6y), > 30 Gy (>6y). Asymmetric irradiation must be avoided. Breast bud in girls < 4y suffers 38% hypoplasia even at 0.34 Gy.
Testes mean dose > 1 Gy causes > 90% oligospermia. Ovaries: < 10 Gy carries 12% POI by age 20y and 50% by 40y; > 10 Gy carries 71% by 20y and 100% by 40y.

entries.title: Toxicity Criteria of the Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) and European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)

grades.Grade_3: Severe symptoms; inpatient admission or urgent intervention

key_passages.text: Acute radiation morbidity occurs within 90 days from the start of radiotherapy; late radiation morbidity occurs greater than 90 days from start of radiotherapy.
